reviews.evidence: Read the complete definition and all sections. Verified the locally compact group, positive linear functional, Haar measure, Lebesgue integral, translations, unimodularity, and modular function links against their canonical targets. Scanner matches for generic functions and measure do not improve the exposition; no prerequisite change.

Read the complete definition and all sections. Verified locally compact group, Borel measure, compact sets, right translation, modular function, Lebesgue measure, probability measure, convolution, and regular representation links. Generic set, group, function, topology, and ambiguous open set matches were rejected as unnecessary or context-sensitive; prerequisites are justified.

Read the complete theorem and sections. Checked reductive group, nonarchimedean local field, admissible representation, test function, distribution, regular semisimple locus, orbital integral, endoscopic transfer, L-packet, stable distribution, and transfer factor links. Rank, measure, object, and regular set scanner suggestions do not represent needed expansions in this context; dependency list matches the theorem setup.

Read the complete definition and sections. Verified real reductive Lie group, Schwartz space, convolution, involution, Xi function, reduced group C-star algebra, Frechet topology, tempered representation, maximal compact subgroup, and spherical transform links. Generic topology, seminorms, derivatives, polynomial, domain, characters, decomposition, and group matches are either already represented by the core or too broad to add; closure is a topology-sensitive ambiguity and remains unlinked.

Read the complete definition and sections. Verified all defining links: real reductive Lie group, maximal compact subgroup, universal enveloping algebra, Lie algebra, Xi function, Frechet space, convolution, coefficient function, and Schwartz-Bruhat space. Scanner suggestions for generic functions, group, polynomial, derivatives, characteristic, and locally compact are not useful at these occurrences; reductive-group matches are field/sense-sensitive and already encoded by the setup.

Read the complete definition and sections. Checked real semisimple group, maximal compact subgroup, minimal parabolic subgroup, spherical principal series, matrix coefficient, Iwasawa projection, restricted roots, probability measure, positive definite function, spherical function, and Harish-Chandra Schwartz space links. Generic function, polynomial, group, and reductive-group candidates do not add reader value; the compact/noncompact convention is explicit.

Read the complete theorem and sections. Verified locally compact group, abelian group, Haar measure, Fourier transform, equivalence class, Lp space, and normalization-dependent arguments. Intersection is a plain set operation in the stated domain; ambiguous interior requires geometric context and is not needed. Generic group/function/norm matches in examples and normalization are intentionally unsaturated; prerequisites are complete.

Read the complete definition and sections. Checked locally compact group, subgroup, Haar measure, convolution, characteristic function, coset, linear representation action, nonarchimedean local field, and maximal compact subgroup links. Generic functions, span, union, decomposition, and group matches are not useful here; reductive group is a field-sensitive contextual phrase and existing setup suffices. No dependency change.

Read the complete theorem and sections. Verified radial-line growth functional, PSH-BM proposition, analytic BM proposition, Paley-Wiener theorem, and Fourier support links. Generic function, derivatives, and sets are mathematical primitives in hypotheses or comparisons, not missing reusable dependencies. The sole prerequisite is the explicitly named radial functional; proof-chain results are ordinary links rather than prerequisites.

Read the complete theorem and sections. Verified porosity on balls, porosity on lines, linear subspaces, damping-function theorem, damping-function FUP theorem, Fourier support, and L2 notation. Measure is used in the explanatory obstruction without defining a measure, and Line porosity is already linked; no new target or prerequisite is justified.
